sections.heading: C — Distractions and fatigue
sections.markdown:
## C — Distractions and fatigue

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A29
Distraction is anything stealing driving attention, and wandering eyes, hands or thoughts all crash alike, even gazing blindly past seen objects. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]
FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A29
Cabin lures span phones, stereos and climate knobs, GPS, DVD screens, dash panels, grooming, chatty riders, loose kids and pets, meals, maps and dropped grabs. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]
FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A29
Roadside lures span traffic gawks, police stops, low sun, roadway people and debris, crash scenes, work zones and billboards. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]
FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A29
Fight back by tabling fights, eating parked, belting kids with toys, crating pets, presetting dials, ignoring far sights, preplanning maps, shunning car chats and headphones, and expecting surprises. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]
FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A29
Spot drifting lanes, yo-yo speeds, fiddling hands, arguing cabins and dawdling rigs, then gift three to four seconds and pass warily past unaware drifters. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]
FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A29
Drivers own every in-car event outright, so distracted crashes blame the wheel holder, never the distraction. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]
FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A29
Fatigue means body or mind tiredness that warps vision, judgment, speed sense, decisions and temper like drink or drugs, and can end asleep at speed. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]
FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A30
Drowsy crash magnets include sixteen to twenty four year olds, apnea sufferers facing sevenfold nod risk, and night or sixty plus hour workers near sixfold risk. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]
FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A30
Pre trip right with seven to nine sleep hours, hundred mile or two hour rest breaks, a relief companion, and zero alcohol or drowsy pills. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]
FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A30
Nod warnings flash as radio cranking and window drops, drooping lids and heads, yawns, lane drifts and missed exits, daydreams, restlessness, dull reactions and fading drive. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]
FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A30
Fight nods by stopping to sleep, napping fifteen to twenty parked minutes, sipping two coffee equivalents ahead of naps without trusting caffeine alone, dodging midnight to six driving, and prizing real sleep most. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]
FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A30
Tired wrecks run solo off roads into rolls or fixed hits, while rumble grooves roar and shake warnings that order instant safe pull offs and alertness checks. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]
FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A30
Colds, infections, aches and many counter or prescription drugs all dull driving, so hand keys over when ill and quiz doctors about risky conditions. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]
FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A30
Worry, thrill, fear, fury and gloom all cloud thinking and tempt risks, so cool off-road, soothe with radio if calm, pad trip time against darting, or cede the wheel. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]

items.why: Sign lists and nap caffeine sequences suit timed recall drills apart from text study.
Habit lists are learned in context with the behavior narrative and need no separate practice mode.

corpus_stability.reason: The Connecticut Driver’s Manual is one dated edition (Revised March 2023, physical p3); nothing on the selected pages indicates more than one rewrite per year.
